Ava — quick internal notes ahead of the kickoff: 

- 8x A100-equivalent is a reasonable starting point for the bulk of Nimbus’s described workload, but we should be explicit about quantization and model choices. If they plan to run 70% 4096-token chat-like prompts we might need to increase to 10 slots or use a higher-memory instance profile to avoid p95 spikes.
- Preliminary perf targets I validated in the lab (mixed 50/50 chat/batch, 1024 avg):
  • 6-slot pool (baseline) — sustainable 250 concurrent streams at p95 ~210ms
  • 8-slot pool — sustainable 350–420 concurrent streams depending on batch window
  • 10-slot pool — sustainable 520 concurrent streams, much more headroom for bursty jobs
- Ops notes: we’ll provision a staging pool with monitoring hooks (token cost exporter, latency histograms) and a pre-populated prompt cache for repeat prefixes.
- Ask for kickoff: please confirm the target 1024-token profile and whether they expect >50% conversational stateful sessions. Also ask Security (Michael Brooks) whether we need extra audit log retention during the eval window.

I’ve attached a short perf worksheet (internal) to the working Drive folder. I’ll be on the kickoff to present runbook and acceptance criteria.

—
Dev Patel
